sentences.text: The Case 1.

The present suit revolves around a long-standing dispute concerning the cultivatory possession of agricultural land situated in Khasra No. 1097 (13 bighas 8 biswas), Village Satbari, Tehsil Saket, New Delhi.
The plaintiff, claims that he has been in continuous cultivatory possession of the suit land since the time of his forefathers.

He contends that despite repeated representations and legal efforts,
the revenue authorities have failed to record his possession in the official land records, particularly in the Khasra Girdawari, which serves as a crucial document reflecting actual cultivatory possession of agricultural land.

2. The dispute primarily arises from administrative inaction and alleged procedural lapses on the part of the Revenue Department, Government of NCT of Delhi, which is responsible for maintaining and updating land records.

The plaintiff asserts that he has repeatedly approached the CS SCJ 639/18 KHUSHI KHAN @ KHUSHI MOHD. Vs. DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (SOUTH) AND ORS.
PAGE NO.2/35 Tehsildar and the SDM Office, submitting various applications to have his cultivatory possession recorded.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further alleges that despite multiple site inspections by revenue officials, their reports confirming his possession have not led to any corrective action in the revenue records.

3. Compounding the issue, the plaintiff claims that third parties have attempted to dispossess him from the land, leading to litigation in the past, where he successfully obtained a decree for permanent injunction against one such individual.

Additionally, the suit land was previously subject to land acquisition proceedings, which were subsequently declared lapsed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

4. On the other hand, the defendants, comprising revenue officials, dispute the plaintiff's claim,
asserting that the suit land falls under Shamlat Deh (common land) or government land, and that the plaintiff is merely an encroacher attempting to establish rights over public property.
They contend that Khasra Girdawari entries are only administrative records that do not confer ownership or tenancy rights and that the plaintiff's suit is an attempt to circumvent due process.

5. The core legal question before the court, therefore, is whether the plaintiff, by virtue of his alleged long-standing cultivatory possession, can seek a mandatory injunction CS SCJ 639/18 KHUSHI KHAN @ KHUSHI MOHD. Vs. DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (SOUTH) AND ORS. PAGE NO.3/35 compelling revenue officials to record his possession in the Khasra Girdawari, or whether such relief is beyond the jurisdiction of a civil court.

The Plaint 7.

The Plaintiff, a farmer by profession and a permanent resident of Village Satbari, New Delhi, has been in actual, physical, and cultivatory possession of shamlat land measuring 13 bighas 8 biswas,
comprising Khasra No. 1097, situated in the revenue estate of Village Satbari, Tehsil Saket, New Delhi.
This land, hereinafter referred to as the suit land, has been under the uninterrupted possession of the Plaintiff's forefathers for generations and is depicted in red in the annexed site plan.
CS SCJ 639/18 KHUSHI KHAN @ KHUSHI MOHD.
Vs. DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (SOUTH) AND ORS. PAGE NO.4/35 8.

Before the enactment of the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954, the Plaintiff's grandfather, Shri Fauju,
was in cultivatory possession of the suit land and continued to remain so even after the Act came into force.

Following his demise in 1974, his grandson, the Plaintiff--Shri Khushi Khan, son of Sh.
Majid--took over the cultivatory possession of the suit land.
Despite multiple requests, the Revenue Department failed to update the revenue records to reflect the Plaintiff's rightful possession.

9. The Defendants, being officers of the Revenue Department, Government of N.C.T. of Delhi, are statutorily obligated to maintain accurate land revenue records within the jurisdiction of Tehsil Saket, New Delhi.
However, despite repeated oral and written representations, they have failed in their duty to record the Plaintiff's cultivatory possession in the Khasra Girdawari, as mandated under the rules.
10.Upon learning of this discrepancy, the Plaintiff submitted multiple applications to the Defendants to update the revenue records.

In response to one such application dated 31.08.2009,
Defendant No. 3 called for a report from the area Patwari, who, in his report dated 03.09.2009,
confirmed that the Plaintiff had sown "hajra" crop on the land.

However, the Patwari failed to make an official record, stating that he lacked the necessary directions from senior officers.

12.In the meantime, one Shri Manoj, son of Ranjit Singh, a resident of Village Chandan Hola, New Delhi, along with his henchmen, attempted to dispossess the Plaintiff from the suit land.

The Written Statement 21.The present suit, though framed as one for mandatory injunction, is in reality an attempt to seek a declaration of Bhumidari rights, which falls exclusively within the jurisdiction of the Revenue Assistant/SDM.
Therefore, this Court lacks jurisdiction to entertain the matter.
The Plaintiff has not approached this Court with clean hands and has suppressed material facts that are crucial to the adjudication of this case.
On this ground alone, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
22.Furthermore, the Plaintiff has no valid cause of action against the Defendants, making the present suit legally untenable.
It is a clear misuse of the process of law, initiated with malafide intent to encroach upon Government land.

The Plaintiff has been persistently attempting to occupy Shamlat Deh (common land), which is meant for the use of CS SCJ 639/18 KHUSHI KHAN @

sentences.text: Since the Plaintiff has no ownership, title, or legal rights over the suit land, the suit is frivolous and without merit.
23.The
Plaintiff's claim of possessing ownership rights over the suit land is wholly incorrect.
The Plaintiff is nothing more than an illegal encroacher, with no legal title, interest, or right of possession.

The suit land is Shamlat Deh (common land) and has been recorded as such in the Khushi Khan @Khushi Mohd vs Deputy Commissioner (South) And Ors on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111304569/
5 revenue records for the use of the village community and the public at large.

sentences.text: The Plaintiff's attempt to establish exclusive ownership over common land is, therefore, legally impermissible.
24.The
allegations that the Plaintiff has been in settled possession of the suit land are completely false and misleading.
The Plaintiff has, on multiple occasions, tried to encroach upon Government land and is now attempting to secure a judicial stamp on his unlawful activities.
There is no basis to the claim that the Plaintiff has been in continuous possession, nor is there any evidence to support such an assertion.
25.The suit land has always been recorded in the name of the Land and Building Department, as evidenced by the Jamabandi for the year 2007-08.

Furthermore, the Khasra Girdawari for 2017-18 clearly reflects that the land remains under the possession of the Land and Building Department,
thereby refuting the Plaintiff's assertion of personal ownership.
CS SCJ 639/18 KHUSHI KHAN @ KHUSHI MOHD.
Vs. DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (SOUTH) AND ORS. PAGE NO.10/35
26.Despite
the Plaintiff's claims
, there is no legal or factual basis to support the contention that he has acquired rights over the suit land.
The entire premise of the suit is built on falsehoods and an attempt to manipulate the legal system to gain unlawful possession of Government land.
The Plaintiff has no legal basis to demand the entry of his name in the Khasra Girdawari, as he was never the rightful occupant of the land.
27.The
claim that a cause of action exists in favor of the Plaintiff is also misleading.
At no point in time has any legal right accrued to the Plaintiff, nor has he been subjected to any violation of legally recognized ownership or possessory rights.
The suit is nothing more than an attempt to undermine public ownership and misuse the legal process for private gains.
28.It is also evident that the Plaintiff has undervalued the suit for the purpose of court fees and jurisdiction, which further renders the suit defective.

Given that the suit property is common land,
the Plaintiff has no right to seek exclusive possession, and the suit must fail on this ground alone.
The prayer clause in the plaint is equally misconceived and baseless.
The reliefs sought are contrary to law, and the Plaintiff cannot claim what is legally impermissible.

sentences.text: Defendants have failed to produce any contrary evidence disproving the Plaintiff's actual cultivatory possession.
Their main argument rests on the contention that the land is recorded as shamlat deh and belongs to the government.
However, it is a well-settled legal principle that mere revenue entries do not override actual possession, particularly when court orders and official reports confirm the possession of the Plaintiff.
86.The
Plaintiff seeks a mandatory injunction directing the Defendants to correct the Khasra Girdawari entries in his favor.

This Court finds that the Revenue Department has been inconsistent in recording the Plaintiff's possession despite confirmations from official inspections; the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, in WP(C) No. 55/2015, had already declared that acquisition proceedings regarding the suit land had lapsed, meaning the land was no longer under government acquisition.

87.Since the revenue authorities have a statutory duty to maintain accurate records of possession,
and their failure has caused legal hardship to the Plaintiff, this Court is duty- bound to ensure compliance with the law.
88.The Defendants argue that the matter falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Revenue Assistant/SDM.
However the Plaintiff is not seeking ownership or bhumidari rights but merely the correction of factual revenue records.

Civil Courts have jurisdiction in cases CS SCJ 639/18 KHUSHI KHAN @ KHUSHI MOHD. Vs. DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (SOUTH) AND ORS. PAGE NO.33/35 where administrative inaction leads to the denial of lawful rights.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The plaintiff, claims that he has been in continuous cultivatory possession of the suit land since the time of his forefathers.
He contends that despite repeated representations and legal efforts,
the revenue authorities have failed to record his possession in the official land records, particularly in the Khasra Girdawari, which serves as a crucial document reflecting actual cultivatory possession of agricultural land.
Before the enactment of the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954, the Plaintiff's grandfather, Shri Fauju,
was in cultivatory possession of the suit land and continued to remain so even after the Act came into force.
Following his demise in 1974, his grandson, the Plaintiff--Shri Khushi Khan, son of Sh.
Majid--took over the cultivatory possession of the suit land.
Despite multiple requests, the Revenue Department failed to update the revenue records to reflect the Plaintiff's rightful possession.
9. The Defendants, being officers of the Revenue Department, Government of N.C.T. of Delhi, are statutorily obligated to maintain accurate land revenue records within the jurisdiction of Tehsil Saket, New Delhi.
However, despite repeated oral and written representations, they have failed in their duty to record the Plaintiff's cultivatory possession in the Khasra Girdawari, as mandated under the rules.
Apprehending forcible eviction, the Plaintiff filed a suit for permanent injunction, restraining Shri Manoj and his associates from illegally dispossessing him.
The suit was decreed in the Plaintiff's favor by Hon'ble Civil Judge Shri Ajay Pandey.
When the Plaintiff approached the Deputy Commissioner (South) on 23.11.2016, the field staff once again confirmed the Plaintiff's possession, yet no corrective action was taken.
16.In 2011, the Plaintiff filed an RTI application, in response to which it was confirmed that the Plaintiff had constructed 4- 5 rooms as cattle sheds on the suit land, and gram/chana crops had been sown in the remaining area.
Despite this official confirmation, the Defendants continued to ignore their statutory obligation to correct the revenue records.
17.Having exhausted all available administrative remedies, the Plaintiff filed a writ petition (WP(C)
No. 4833/2017) before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, which directed Defendant No. 1 to treat the writ petition along with annexures as a representation and dispose of the same by a speaking order within eight weeks.
However, the Defendants failed to comply with this judicial directive, prompting the Plaintiff to submit a written request to the Deputy Commissioner (South) on 24.10.2017, which also remained unaddressed.
However, the Plaintiff continued to retain physical possession.
The Written Statement 21.The present suit, though framed as one for mandatory injunction, is in reality an attempt to seek a declaration of Bhumidari rights, which falls exclusively within the jurisdiction of the Revenue Assistant/SDM.
Before the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954, PW-1's grandfather, Shri Fauju (son of Sh. Dhundal), was in cultivatory possession of the land and continued to cultivate it even after the Act came into force.
PW-1 filed a suit for permanent injunction, and the Hon'ble Civil Judge, Shri Ajay Pandey, decreed the suit in favor of PW-1 on 02.06.2011, confirming his lawful possession.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Additionally, the suit land was previously subject to land acquisition proceedings, which were subsequently declared lapsed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
4. On the other hand, the defendants, comprising revenue officials, dispute the plaintiff's claim,
asserting that the suit land falls under Shamlat Deh (common land) or government land, and that the plaintiff is merely an encroacher attempting to establish rights over public property.
Plaintiff contends that he has been in continuous, uninterrupted physical and cultivatory possession of the suit land since the time of his forefathers.
Defendants have failed to produce any contrary evidence disproving the Plaintiff's actual cultivatory possession.
Their main argument rests on the contention that the land is recorded as shamlat deh and belongs to the government.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Plaintiff has not approached this Court with clean hands and has suppressed material facts that are crucial to the adjudication of this case.
On this ground alone, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
22.Furthermore, the Plaintiff has no valid cause of action against the Defendants, making the present suit legally untenable.
It is a clear misuse of the process of law, initiated with malafide intent to encroach upon Government land.
The Plaintiff has been persistently attempting to occupy Shamlat Deh (common land), which is meant for the use of CS SCJ 639/18 KHUSHI KHAN @
KHUSHI MOHD. Vs. DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (SOUTH) AND ORS. PAGE NO.9/35 the entire village community.
Since the Plaintiff has no ownership, title, or legal rights over the suit land, the suit is frivolous and without merit.
Plaintiff's claim of possessing ownership rights over the suit land is wholly incorrect.
The Plaintiff is nothing more than an illegal encroacher, with no legal title, interest, or right of possession.
The Plaintiff's attempt to establish exclusive ownership over common land is, therefore, legally impermissible.
allegations that the Plaintiff has been in settled possession of the suit land are completely false and misleading.
The Plaintiff has, on multiple occasions, tried to encroach upon Government land and is now attempting to secure a judicial stamp on his unlawful activities.
There is no basis to the claim that the Plaintiff has been in continuous possession, nor is there any evidence to support such an assertion.
25.The suit land has always been recorded in the name of the Land and Building Department, as evidenced by the Jamabandi for the year 2007-08.
, there is no legal or factual basis to support the contention that he has acquired rights over the suit land.
The entire premise of the suit is built on falsehoods and an attempt to manipulate the legal system to gain unlawful possession of Government land.
The Plaintiff has no legal basis to demand the entry of his name in the Khasra Girdawari, as he was never the rightful occupant of the land.
claim that a cause of action exists in favor of the Plaintiff is also misleading.
At no point in time has any legal right accrued to the Plaintiff, nor has he been subjected to any violation of legally recognized ownership or possessory rights.
The suit is nothing more than an attempt to undermine public ownership and misuse the legal process for private gains.
87.Since the revenue authorities have a statutory duty to maintain accurate records of possession,
and their failure has caused legal hardship to the Plaintiff, this Court is duty- bound to ensure compliance with the law.
